artworks.title: Anius and Aeneas
artworks.description: Print of Anius receiving Aeneas on Delos — Apollo's son and priest-king hosting the Trojan exile as Virgil tells in Aeneid 3.

artworks.title: Armorial Dish: The Story of King Anius
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum istoriato dish titled for King Anius — the Delian host whose wine, wheat and oil daughters feed the Trojan fleet.

artworks.title: Armorial Dish: The Story of King Anius (alternate)
artworks.description: Second photograph of the Anius maiolica — Renaissance tableware that made the Delian king a dining-room myth.

artworks.title: Daughters of Anius Changed into Doves
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print: Anius' daughters transformed into doves — Ovid's sequel when Agamemnon's Greeks try to seize the girls who feed armies.

artworks.title: Aeneas on Delos
artworks.description: Drawing of Aeneas' stop at Delos — Anius' island sanctuary where the Trojan remnant hears Apollo's oracle of Italy.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Virgil seats Anius as priest-king of Delos who hosts Aeneas and Anchises — the Delian friend whose hospitality opens Book 3.

popCulture.title: Anius
popCulture.description: Son of Apollo, king of Delos — father of the wine-, grain- and oil-giving daughters; not the metalmark butterfly of the same name.
